jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Professional Trust
jokes.joke: I worked as a celebrity’s personal assistant, which is basically a job where every instruction ends with, “Don’t ask questions.” One day he handed me a sealed envelope and said, “Take this across town and give it only to Marco.” I said, “What’s in it?” He said, “You’re happier not knowing.” That’s when I realized my employee benefits included plausible deniability.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Earpiece of Faith
jokes.joke: I was a celebrity's personal assistant for a week. Just an earpiece feeding me instructions I couldn't question. "Tell the driver left." Left. "Tell security he's her cousin." Cousin. At one point the voice said "tell the crowd she's not coming, but say it like it's good news," and I did it, I smiled and said "great news, everybody," and four hundred strangers cheered nothing. That's the job. You don't get answers. You get a voice in your ear and the terrifying privilege of never once asking why.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: The Wage Gap
jokes.joke: I used to be a personal assistant to a pretty major celebrity. That whole dynamic relies entirely on blind trust. Every night at the club, he’d hand me his unlocked phone, his black card, and his car keys. He just completely trusted that a guy making seventeen dollars an hour wasn't going to Venmo himself five grand and text his publicist that we were in love.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Celebrity PA Duties
jokes.joke: I landed a job as the personal assistant to a celebrity and every day is pure cringe. Yesterday they made me rehearse their award speech in the kitchen so they could 'feel the emotion from a distance.' There I am holding a spatula like a trophy, eyes watering, saying 'this means the world.' They walked in, nodded, and said, 'Good energy. Next time try less spatula.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: VIP Instructions
jokes.joke: I got a job as a personal assistant to a celebrity, which is basically a full-time experiment in blindly trusting someone richer than me. On my first day she texted, “Take my goat to a sound bath.” I thought it was a typo, but when your boss owns a goat and a sound bath, the typo is assuming you're the normal one.
